rows.text: Warsaw, 8 July 2026
Information from the meeting of the Monetary Policy Council held on 7-8 July 2026
The Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged:
▪ reference rate at 3.75%;
▪ lombard rate at 4.25%;
▪ deposit rate at 3.25%;
▪ rediscount rate at 3.80%;
▪ discount rate at 3.85%.
Prices of energy commodities in the global markets decreased over the last month, with the fall in oil prices being significant.

At the same time, the economic activity growth in the immediate environment of the Polish economy is still subdued and inflation – despite a recent decline – is higher than at the beginning of the year.
The outlook for global activity and inflation is subject to uncertainty, stemming, in particular, from the conflict in the Middle East.
In Poland, in May 2026 retail sales, industrial output as well as construction and assembly production increased in annual terms.
Annual wage growth in the enterprise sector in May 2026 was lower than in 2026 Q1 and employment in this part of the economy was still declining.
According to the Statistics Poland flash estimate, in June 2026 CPI inflation decreased to 2.5% y/y (against 3.1% y/y in May).
This was mainly due to the decline in the annual growth in prices of fuels for personal transport equipment as well as food and non-alcoholic beverages.
The Council became acquainted with the results of the July projection of inflation and GDP based on the NECMOD model.

In line with the projection, prepared under the assumption of unchanged NBP interest rates and taking into account data available until 17 June 2026, there is a 50-percent probability that the annual price growth will be in the range of 2.4 – 3.3% in 2026 (against 1.6 – 2.9% in the March 2026 projection), 1.5 – 4.0% in 2027 (compared to 1.1 – 3.7%) and 0.8 – 3.9% in 2028 (compared to 0.9 – 4.0%).

At the same time, the annual GDP growth – according to the projection – will be with a 50-percent probability in the range of 3.0 – 4.4% in 2026 (against 3.1 – 4.7% in the March 2026 projection), 1.8 – 3.7% in 2027 (compared to 2.0 – 3.8%) and 1.9 – 4.1% in 2028 (compared to 1.8 – 4.1%).
Against this background the Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged.
Further decisions of the Council will depend on incoming information regarding prospects for inflation and economic activity in Poland.
Particularly important is macroeconomic situation abroad, including developments in global commodity prices and inflation, amid changing geopolitical context.
The shape of fiscal policy, changes in activity growth of the Polish economy and further developments in wage growth also remain risk factors for inflation outlook.

NBP will continue to take all necessary actions in order to ensure macroeconomic and financial stability, including above all to keep inflation at the level consistent with the NBP inflation target in the medium term.
NBP may intervene in the foreign exchange market.
